title: Volkswagen workers protest cutbacks at Emden wage talks
seoTitle: Emden Volkswagen workers protest wage cuts

tea.why: Volkswagen proposed severe cost-cutting measures, including pay freezes, job cuts, plant closure threats, and longer working hours.
tea.want: IG Metall demands a 5% wage increase and guarantees for jobs and factory futures.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Initial wage negotiations in Emden ended without agreement after 1.5 hours.

summary: Thousands of Volkswagen employees gathered outside the Nordseehalle in Emden on 24 November 2026 to protest proposed cost-cutting measures as company management and union representatives met for initial tariff negotiations. Organized by IG Metall, the demonstration featured banners, horns, red smoke flares, and symbolic black wooden coffins representing the future of the company. Protesters opposed Volkswagen's proposals, which included freezing wages for 2027 and 2028, cutting bonuses, paring back the 35-hour work week, and potential plant closures. IG Metall demanded a five percent wage increase and protection for jobs and production sites. Police estimated turnout at 2,300 people, while IG Metall reported around 4,500 participants. The negotiations ended without progress after about 90 minutes, with management emphasizing the need for cost reductions to preserve industrial jobs.
demands: Protection of employment and plant sites
Rejection of wage freezes and benefit cuts
response: Volkswagen management stated that cost-reduction measures are necessary to maintain as many industrial jobs as possible and called for a quick agreement without losing time.

crowd.text: around 4,500 people according to IG Metall (police estimated about 2,300)

updates.text: Volkswagen workers demonstrated in Emden outside tariff negotiations with management.
The 90-minute initial negotiation round between IG Metall and Volkswagen ended without an agreement.
